I'll dig into the incident records. Let me start with a few parallel searches.

Let me read the postmortem, the customer-facing incident report, and the incident channel thread in full.

Let me check the status of the remediation tickets and the fix PR.

**Thursday Nov 12 (SEV2, 08:47–12:27 UTC, 3h40 of stale dashboards)** [1]

**What broke.** The v2.14.0 deploy (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB, but the ingest-worker pods only have a 512 Mi memory limit — so on the first large batch they went OOM and crash-looped, and the change hit all pods at once [1][3][9]. A Kafka broker-disk hypothesis was raised early and ruled out at 09:41 (disk was at 62%) [3].

**Was customer data lost? No.** Events kept arriving in Kafka and were only processed late. Reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed per-workspace event counts matched Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC — "nothing lost, just late" [1][3]. Impact was delayed dashboards for all workspaces, with 4 customers contacting support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trials); Maya sent incident reports to Orbitly and Zest on Nov 15 [1][2]. Note the commercial side: Orbitly is claiming an SLA service credit under section 7 of their MSA, and Sam is still checking terms with finance — their signed MSA isn't attached to the HubSpot deal [2][7].

**Detection was the weak point:** there was no consumer-lag alert. The first signal was a Sentry OOM alert at 09:14, 27 minutes after deploy [1][9].

**Changes we're making:**
- Alert on consumer lag > 5 min, routed to on-call — KES-431, Noa, due Nov 20. The rule is live but still being tuned because 5 min fires on every nightly backfill; stays In Progress until quiet for 3 nights [1][10]
- Config changes go to a canary pool first — KES-432, Daniel, due Nov 27. The ingest#419 fix itself was shipped as v2.14.1 through canary [1][6]
- Raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes — KES-433, Lior, due Nov 27 [1]
- Code fix merged Nov 13 (ingest#419): default `max_batch_bytes` back to 1 MB, plus a batcher guard that refuses batches over 25% of the container memory limit and warns; the bulk import path keeps 10 MB explicitly since it runs on the 2 Gi pool [1][6]

**Also changed:** the Postgres 17 cutover was moved from Nov 21 to Dec 5, after the Fernhill go-live, to avoid stacking a DB migration on a fresh incident [5][15].

Two caveats: I couldn't find the current status of KES-432 and KES-433 in Linear — only KES-431 has updates [10]. And the cause took ~54 minutes to identify, but the rollback itself was fast once found (13 minutes) [1].
